malign

muh-LINE · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To malign is to speak evil of someone to damage their reputation.

The rival campaign maligned her record with false accusations.

Worked Example

The tabloid maligned the actress for years with rumors that were later proven completely false.

Deliberately spreading harmful, often false claims about someone's character is exactly what malign describes.

Your Turn

Answer correctly to continue.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

slander: To slander is to make false spoken statements that damage someone's reputation -- in law, the spoken twin of libel. To malign covers more ground: any deliberate speaking of evil about a person, whether or not the claims could ever reach a courtroom.

badmouth: To badmouth is casual, everyday talking-down -- unfair complaints about someone made behind their back, at whatever small scale. To malign is graver: it means deliberately speaking evil of a person, seriously enough to stain their reputation.

smear: To smear is to run an organized public attack on someone's good name -- untrue stories planted in the press, rumors pushed to a wide audience. To malign is broader and can be quieter: one person deliberately speaking evil of another, in public or not.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

praise: express approval or admiration

vindicate: clear someone of blame or suspicion

Where it sits · how unfair and damaging the talk — criticize → malign → defame

criticize vs. malign: To criticize can be fair and honest; to malign someone is to deliberately speak evil of them, often unfairly.

defame vs. malign: Defame goes further than malign, often carrying the specific legal implication of damaging someone's reputation with false statements.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — mal-

prefix — mal-: bad (Latin (malus))

suffix — -ign

suffix — -ign: born, produced (Latin (gignere))

Put it together

Put it together: mal- ('bad') + -ign ('born, produced') together suggest something 'badly born' -- an old way of describing a harmful nature, now the deliberate slander malign describes.

Use the root in a new word: malice

Use the root in a new word: malice: Malice comes from the same Latin root, mal- ('bad'), that opens malign.
